A little about me

I care about the moments where people get stuck

My approach

I've spent the past few years working on banking, payments, marketplaces and AI products. The projects look different, but the questions I ask are usually the same: who is this for, and what is getting in their way?

I enjoy getting involved early, sketching rough ideas and talking them through with developers. A neat Figma file is only part of the job.

At Horal I designed for buyers and sellers. At Radius I worked on payments for students and their families. At ITSS I helped design Vista banking across four markets, and at Bizinc I grew into a design leadership role.

I'm also studying for an MSc in User Experience Design at the University of Brighton. It's a chance to keep questioning my assumptions and get better at the decisions behind the screens.

BEYOND THE SCREEN

I’m curious about the details most people overlook.

On Radius, that meant thinking about someone trying to pay a student’s fees from another country. On Vista, it meant making sure a finance manager could tell which company they were acting for. Different products, but the same feeling: an important decision should never have to be a guessing game.

I’m now studying UX Design at the University of Brighton, and I still enjoy getting into the technical side of how things are built. Outside the screen, football is a good reminder that teamwork and practice matter there too.

Design values

How I approach design

Clarity

Curiosity

Ask a better question before rushing into a solution.

Integrity

Be clear about what I did and what the evidence really says.

Collaboration

Keep everyone in the loop, especially when things change.
